01-1.caption: Tycho Brahe's great mural quadrant at Uraniborg: Tycho is painted on the wall inside the arc while assistants observe and record.

01-2.author: Ziegler175
01-2.caption: The curved twin stone track of Ulugh Beg's giant underground sextant in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, built in the 1420s.

01-3.author: Copernican_heliocentrism_diagram.jpg: Own work from Copernicus 1543 derivative work: Professor marginalia (talk)
01-3.caption: Copernicus's 1543 diagram from De revolutionibus: the Sun (Sol) in the middle, circled by the planets and Earth with its Moon.

02-1.author: Geni
02-1.caption: The Nimrud lens, a polished oval of rock crystal about 3,000 years old from Assyria, in the British Museum.

02-2.file: Tommaso da modena, ritratti di domenicani (Ugo di Provenza) 1352 150cm, treviso, ex convento di san niccolò, sala del capitolo (cropped).jpg
02-2.author: Tommaso da Modena
02-2.caption: Tommaso da Modena's 1352 fresco in Treviso: Cardinal Hugh of Saint-Cher writing with spectacles on his nose, the oldest known painting of glasses.

02-3.file: I.A. Haitham, Diagram of the eye, 16th century Wellcome L0011969.jpg
02-3.author: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/obf_images/84/c0/294ed3a58d42ea52d8d1ddee5981.jpg Gallery: https://wellcomeimages.org/indexplus/image/L
02-3.caption: A diagram of the eye and optic nerve from a 16th-century printed Latin edition of Ibn al-Haytham's Book of Optics.

03-1.author: Jacob van Meurs
03-1.caption: An old engraved portrait of Hans Lipperhey, the Middelburg spectacle maker who asked for the first telescope patent in 1608.

03-2.author: Thomas Harriot
03-2.caption: Thomas Harriot's drawing of the crescent Moon seen through a telescope on 26 July 1609, months before Galileo's.

03-3.author: Astrodidge
03-3.caption: How a Galilean telescope works: a convex front lens (L1) and a concave eyepiece (L2) bend light rays into a bigger image.

04-1.author: Galileo Galilei
04-1.caption: Galileo's ink-wash drawings of the Moon from 1609, showing craters and the ragged line between light and shadow.

04-2.file: Sample of Sidereus Nuncius drawings of Jupiter and the Medicean Stars (medicean stars iautheme).jpg
04-2.author: History of Science Collections, University of Oklahoma Libraries
04-2.caption: Part of a page of Sidereus Nuncius (1610): Galileo's sketches of Jupiter (circle) with its moons (stars) on different nights.

04-3.file: Galilei telescopes, Museo Galileo, Florence, Inv. 242, 2428, 224088.jpg
04-3.author: Zde
04-3.caption: Galileo's two surviving telescopes, made around 1609-1610, on display at the Museo Galileo in Florence.

05-1.author: The Galileo Project/M. Kornmesser
05-1.caption: Galileo's drawing of sunspots on the Sun's disk, made on 23 June 1612, like those in his 1613 Letters on Sunspots.

05-2.author: Joseph-Nicolas Robert-Fleury
05-2.caption: 'Galileo before the Holy Office' (Robert-Fleury, 1847): an imagined scene of Galileo facing the Inquisition in Rome in 1633.

05-3.author: Giovanni Battista Landini
05-3.caption: Frontispiece and title page of Galileo's Dialogue (Florence, 1632): Aristotle, Ptolemy and Copernicus talking together.
